section_summary.extract_value: This section reports preliminary data analyses assessing normality (skewness and kurtosis) and multicollinearity (VIF). It states skewness values ranged from −0.16 (BAS-2) to 1.84 (Age), kurtosis values ranged between −0.40 (BAS-2) and 4.52 (Age), and VIF values ranged between 0.05 (Age) and 1.16 (OAS). The section does not mention study numbering, sample size, demographics, BMI values, assessment methods, or correlations between body appreciation and BMI.
section_summary.evidence_source: First of all, the suitability of the data for further statistical analyses was tested. The normality of data distribution was confirmed through the analysis of coefficients of Skewness and Kurtosis. Values of Skewness ranged from −0.16 (BAS-2) to 1.84 (Age), and Kurtosis values between −0.40 (BAS-2) and 4.52 (Age), which do not suggest the presence of serious violation of normal distribution, according to Kline (2005). Furthermore, Variance Inflation Factor (VIF) values ranged between 0.05 (Age) and 1.16 (OAS), which indicates a low probability of multicollinearity issues (Kline, 2005).

section_summary.extract_value: This section reports preliminary data analyses: tests of normality using skewness and kurtosis (skewness range: −0.16 for BAS-2 to 1.84 for Age; kurtosis range: −0.40 for BAS-2 to 4.52 for Age) indicating no serious violation of normality, and VIF values (0.05 for Age to 1.16 for OAS) indicating low multicollinearity. The accompanying figure (Fig. 1) shows a final path model with standardized path coefficients among Age, OAS, BMI, SCS_SC, and BAS-2. The section does not label any study as 'Study 1' nor describe multiple studies.
